metadata.case_name: FUNG SIU FUN v. LI LUNG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: clerical capacity at former school (offer mentioned)

injuries.icd_description: Fracture of skull or facial bones, part unspecified

injuries.description: Fractures of the left pelvic bone.
source: Fractures of the left pelvic bone.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of unspecified pelvic bone without disruption of posterior arch of pelvic ring

injuries.description: Fracture of the shaft of the right femur.
source: Fracture of the shaft of the right femur.

manifestations.description: Occasional headaches and a loss of concentration with some lapses of memory (described as "mild post-concussion syndrome").
Some slight tenderness reported by Dr. R.G.M. Wedderburn when pressure is applied to the scar.
Inability to read for any longer period than thirty minutes and confinement to the house; boredom.
Permanent discomfort and pain if she should walk or stand for too long (displacement after pelvic fractures).
Expected osteo-arthritic changes which will further deteriorate her condition.
Permanent stiffness particularly to the right knee (resulting from fracture of the right femur fixed with a plate and screws).
Unable to stand for any lengthy period without feeling discomfort; injuries to the lower part of her body restrict her ability to undertake many simple household tasks.

treatments_received: Initially admitted to Tang Shiu Kin Hospital
Referred to Queen Mary Hospital where she remained for three months
Transferred to Sandy Bay Convalescent Home
Open reduction and internal fixation by a long metal plate secured by six screws

losses.description: Will be a partial cripple for the rest of her life; permanent discomfort and pain on walking or standing for long periods.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Inability to perform numerous household tasks; requires future employment of a part-time amah at $300 per month.
Unable to return to full-time teaching; has advertised as a private tutor without success; offered clerical employment at former school on a salary of $550 p.m.
Confinement to the house and boredom resulting from inability to read for more than thirty minutes and other restrictions.
